problem_text:
A logistics company must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a critical component across a 16-week operational timeline.  
The starting stock at the opening of the timeline is 7 units.  
In each week \( t = 1, \dots, 16 \), the vendor permits the company to issue a purchase request whose size must fall between 10 and 52 units.  
Nevertheless, every request issued will undergo a 4‑week lead time before it becomes available to meet requirements or rebuild stock.  
The requirement for the component in each week is provided as follows:  
* Week 1: requirement 25 units  
* Week 2: requirement 12 units  
* Week 3: requirement 50 units  
* Week 4: requirement 27 units  
* Week 5: requirement 26 units  
* Week 6: requirement 34 units  
* Week 7: requirement 17 units  
* Week 8: requirement 32 units  
* Week 9: requirement 28 units  
* Week 10: requirement 33 units  
* Week 11: requirement 49 units  
* Week 12: requirement 50 units  
* Week 13: requirement 22 units  
* Week 14: requirement 57 units  
* Week 15: requirement 44 units  
* Week 16: requirement 44 units  

Stock‑outs are tolerated, but any unsatisfied requirement will not be deferred to later weeks.  
Throughout the timeline, component quantities may be fractional, and the total quantity of physical stock on hand at any moment must not surpass the storage‑facility limit of 50 units.  
The aggregate expense over the timeline comprises three elements: the procurement expense, which amounts to 1 per unit requested; the storage expense, which amounts to 1 per unit of stock retained from one week to the next; and the shortage penalty, which amounts to 13 per unit of unfulfilled requirement.  
Identify the optimal purchase quantity for each week and monitor the consequent stock and shortage levels so as to minimize the total expense.
